experiences.name: Interdisciplinary Institute of Political Economy (IIEP - UBA - CONICET)
experiences.summary:
I assisted in research projects that aimed to extract U.S. inflation expectations from 'the market' (a pool of U.S. firms), through the use of synthetic surveys completed using Machine Learning techniques.
I worked as a part of a research team, where my tasks focused on building databases, developing and reviewing code, and participating in the fine-tuning process of the models.
My work was supervised by José Daniel Aromí (Ph.D., University of Maryland).

experiences.name: ZS (consulting)
experiences.summary:
At ZS, I specialize in data analytics, automation, and process optimization for complex business environments, with a focus on pharmaceutical-sector analytics.
My work centers on transforming high-volume commercial, operational, and de-identified patient-level datasets into reliable, structured, and decision-ready outputs. I combine Python, SQL, and analytical thinking to build reproducible workflows that improve data quality, reduce manual intervention, and strengthen the traceability of critical business processes.
I contributed to the automation of a complex end-to-end analytics workflow, reducing processing time from approximately one month to one week while materially improving output reliability. By replacing manual, error-prone steps with reproducible logic and validation layers, the process became faster, more transparent, and substantially less dependent on downstream restatements.
Beyond analysis, I focus on designing systems that make analytics faster, safer, and more scalable. This includes standardizing fragmented data sources, improving workflow governance, and creating analytical outputs that support reporting, simulation, strategic planning, and data-driven business decisions.

experiences.name: [NDA protected] through consulting firm
experiences.summary:
I worked as a freelance Geospatial Data Analyst for a client in the Telecommunications industry through a specialized consulting firm, under a Non-Disclosure Agreement.
My work focused on analyzing and visualizing spatial data for real-world applications, particularly using basic network theory concepts and visualizations. Other type of visualizations, such as heatmaps to identify hotspots or underserved areas, were also part of the tasks to complete.
I primarily used R (and its most common libraries for spatial analysis) but I relied on other tools -such as ArcGIS and Python- as a backup.

Note: due to the nature of the project, detailed information is protected by the NDA. However, I am currently working on a mock project using similar techniques as the ones I used for this job, only this time with public and randomized data. I am happy to discuss the technologies and approaches I used in a general context.

projects.name: Econ
projects.summary: I conducted multiple data analyses of economic data, whether in the form of personal side-projects or by-products of ongoing research. This is a collection of a tiny fraction of those analyses.

projects.name: TTS
projects.summary: I built a fully local voice-cloning pipeline that turns Jupyter notebooks into synchronized lecture videos, narrated by a fine-tuned clone of my own voice. It combines a fine-tuned XTTS v2 model, an automated JupyterLab session driven by Playwright and the Jupyter kernel WebSocket protocol, and inline timestamp synchronization. Ten numbered scripts, no external API calls at run time.

projects.name: BCRA_bot
projects.summary:
I developed a Twitter bot (@BCRA_bot) that tweets daily updates of Argentina's monetary statistics, together with weekly and monthly analyses. Data is gathered using the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA)'s official API.
The bot is hosted in Google Cloud Platform, and run with Google Cloud Scheduler.

projects.name: EcoBici
projects.summary: I conducted a comprehensive data analysis of EcoBici, the public bike-sharing program of Buenos Aires to assess how, when and why people use the service. It includes mapping of most popular rides, as well as a thorough analysis. The project is now turning into an impact evaluation approach.

projects.name: Ma-py-tas
projects.summary: Along the years, I created multiple maps as part of a geospatial data science project I proposed to myself. The topics included are diverse, and so are the formats of data: from a simple GeoJSON to web scraping latitudes and longitudes, and everything in between.
